changes.evidence: Eyes of Wakanda episode 2 ('Legends and Lies'): B'Kai has served undercover as 'Memnon' for nine years in the Greek army, fighting beside Achilles as one of the Myrmidons (the name is said on screen: Odysseus, 'Won't be long now before the Myrmidons open the gates'). He turns on them, kills Achilles, and takes the pendant home to Wakanda and the War Dogs (Hatut Zaraze). The owner's rules count undercover service (Natasha's Stark Industries stage in Iron Man 2 is the precedent). The MCU wiki lists Myrmidons as a former affiliation.

Marvel Zombies episode 2: Zemo leads the survivor community on the Raft and tries to feed Kamala's group to Namor. After Namor destroys the Raft, Zemo escapes in the life pod with the heroes ('forced to team up with the heroes'). In episode 3 he travels with them to New Asgard and is killed there by an infected Asgardian. He ends his story with the survivors, and death is not a departure, so the 'left' and the Independent stage don't hold. John Walker, his partner in the betrayal, is filed as The Survivors with no left.

groups: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

changes.evidence: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier episode 1: the U.S. Air Force sends Sam on the Tunisia hijacking mission under Major Hill, with USAF First Lieutenant Torres as his support. He keeps working with them through the series (the MCU wiki's 'Return to the Military' section: 'With the Avengers disbanded, Wilson returned to working with the United States Air Force ... as an independent contractor'). The owner's rules count an employer as a group, and joining another group is a move. At the end of Captain America: Brave New World Sam decides to rebuild the Avengers (wiki 'Reassembling the Avengers'), so the Avengers stay his last group. A gpass change (gout_13) found this too, but it was dropped in the backstory revert along with its backstory part. Minimal alternative: add only the FATWS U.S. Air Force stage.

owner_calls.question: In Loki S2 (episodes 3-4), Miss Minutes works with Renslayer against the TVA leadership to retake it for He Who Remains' plan, and crushes Dox's loyalists. O.B.'s reboot shuts her down, and in the finale Ouroboros reprograms her to run the new TVA. Does she turn on the TVA (Independent at Loki S2, then back to The TVA at Loki S2)?
options: [["The TVA","(from the start)"],["Independent","Loki S2"],["The TVA","Loki S2"]]
owner_calls.evidence: MCU wiki 'Seeking Control': she suggests to Renslayer that they don't need He Who Remains to restore stability to the TVA, and Renslayer offers the loyalists a life on the timeline to help her 'retake the Time Variance Authority'. 'New Life': rebooted, she 'resumed her operation of TVA technology'. This is the same open question as the earlier call in out_11.

owner_calls.question: In What If...? S3 (season episodes 6-8), the Order of the Watchers (Eminence, Incarnate, Executioner) capture Uatu for breaking his oath. Guardians rescue him and he fights the Order in the Battle of the Cosmos. The MCU wiki now lists the Order of the Watchers as a 'former' affiliation. Does this end his 'The Watchers' stage?
options: Add a departure in What If...? S3 (Independent, or a new group he forms with Kahhori, Byrdie and Storm)
owner_calls.evidence: Wiki 'Becoming His Own Person': captured by the Order (WI306) and rescued by the Guardians (WI308). The infobox lists 'Order of the Watchers (formerly)'. This is the same open question as the earlier calls in gout_03 and out_27.
